note: This year's sheet uses the department's older 'EE' course prefix throughout, not 'ECE' (the rename happened between the 2023 and 2024 printings). Matches 2022+ on ABET credit totals (30/45) and the 'Systems & Data Sciences (SDS) Track' name/12cr Group I -- both of those changed from the 2020 printing (still 32/48 and plain 'Systems Track' at 11cr there; see checksheets/data/2020.json's own note), so 2021 is the first printing with the values every later sheet also uses. Footnote numbers also differ from 2024+: this sheet has 10 notes, not 11 (see the missing-caveat item in known_ambiguities), same as every other pre-2024 sheet.

gened_codes.FG: Foundations: Global & Multicultural Perspectives (6 cr across two courses; note 1 on the sheet, printed as 'FG Foundation Courses'). Two FG slots of 3 cr each appear on the grid.
gened_codes.W: Writing Intensive. 5 courses required, minimum of 2 in upper division (note 4). Printed as just 'Writing Intensive (W)', not the 'W/WI' form used from 2024 on. Grid shows 'W Focus (5)'.
gened_codes.H: Hawaiian, Asian & Pacific Issues. One course required (note 5). Printed as just 'Hawaiian, Asian & Pacific Issues (H)', not the 'H/HAP' form used from 2024 on -- this sheet also has no equivalent of 2024+'s note stating H is excluded from engineering courses and may double-count with DH/DL/DS; see known_ambiguities. Grid shows 'H Focus (1)'.
gened_codes.O: Oral Communication. One course required (note 5). Printed as just 'Oral Communication (O)'. Grid shows 'O Focus (1)'.
gened_codes.E: Contemporary Ethical Issues. One course required (note 5). Printed as just 'Contemporary Ethical Issues (E)'. Grid shows 'E Focus (1)'.

substitutions: MATH 251, MATH 252, and MATH 253 (the Accelerated Calculus sequence) may substitute for the MATH 241-244 sequence -- a whole-sequence substitution, not a course-by-course one (note 2). Printed without the '-A' suffix used on 2022+ sheets (MATH 251A/252A/253A) -- recorded as printed, not assumed to be the same course numbers.
CHEM 181/181L, or CHEM 171/171L, may substitute for CHEM 161/161L and CHEM 162 (note 3). The sheet doesn't specify whether this is a full 3-for-3 substitution or partial; recorded as printed.
ENGR 196, ENGR 296, and ENGR 396 may substitute for EE 196, EE 296, and EE 396 respectively (note 9).

technical_electives.rule: EE courses numbered 300 or above, totaling 7 additional credits drawn from the track lists (note 8). Of these, 3 credits must be outside the student's chosen major track and 1 credit must be a laboratory. On the grid: TE EE (3 cr, Junior Spring) + TE EE (3 cr) + (Lab) TE EE (1 cr) (both Senior Fall) = 7 cr, matching note 8.

engineering_breadth.rule: Engineering Breadth (EB, 3 cr) is satisfied by a CEE, ME, OE, or BE course at the 300 level or higher; or CEE 270; or a physical/biological/computer science course at the 300 level or higher, which additionally requires approval from the Department's Undergraduate Curriculum Committee (note 7).

concentrations.Biomedical: All Group I courses in either the EP or Systems Track, plus two biomedical-related Group II courses and an EB course approved by the Department's Undergraduate Curriculum Committee and listed on the EE website. EE 496 will be a biomedical project approved by the concentration coordinator.
concentrations.Energy: All Group I courses in either the EP or Systems Track, plus two energy-related Group II courses and an EB course approved by the Department's Undergratuate Curriculum Committee and listed on the EE website. EE 496 will be an energy project approved by the concentration coordinator

other_rules.major_track_minimum: A minimum of 17 credits in one of the major tracks: all track core courses (Group I) plus the remaining track elective courses (Group II).
other_rules.all_courses_letter_graded: ALL COURSES MUST BE TAKEN FOR LETTER (A-F) GRADES.
other_rules.prereq_grade_requirement: Enrollment in EE courses requires a grade of 'C' or better in all prerequisite courses (note 6).
other_rules.alternate_track_proposal: A student, along with a faculty member, may propose an alternate track if (1) equivalent in rigor & breadth to the listed tracks, (2) endorsed by another faculty member, and (3) approved by the Department's Undergraduate Curriculum Committee (note 10).

known_ambiguities: This sheet has no equivalent of the 2024+ note stating that H (Hawaiian, Asian & Pacific Issues) is not included in engineering courses and may double-count with DH/DL or DS. Genuinely absent from this year's notes (confirmed against the full text), not an extraction gap.
Note 8's '3 must be outside the major track' most likely means 3 credits (parallel to '1 [credit] must be a laboratory'), not 3 courses, but the sheet doesn't say so explicitly.

EE 205 is listed as TE-eligible (note 8) despite being below the stated '300 or above' threshold for Technical Electives -- the same inconsistency present in every other year's sheet, not a transcription error.
CHEM 171/171L or CHEM 181/181L vs. CHEM 161/161L + CHEM 162: the sheet doesn't specify if this is a full-scope or partial substitution.
